summary: Imagine Mars Transit Day 142: a sudden solar proton storm hits while Earth is up to 44 minutes away by radio, making AstraHealth on the cabin tablet the crew’s instant, autonomous AI Flight Surgeon before Mission Control even receives the distress signal. Beyond Earth, continuous radiation (1.8 mSv/day), rapid bone loss (up to 1.5%/mo), prolonged blackouts, missing-exam fake-zero bugs, and slow power-hungry cloud or 2B+ LLMs cost astronauts the critical 5–15 minute evacuation window. To close this gap, AstraHealth moves clinical triage onto an offline-first React + localStorage edge architecture synced asynchronously via DTN (NASA MCP + OpenFDA), pairing a 0.67 MB LightGBM ONNX early-warning model (22 ms p95), a deterministic <0.02 ms NASA-STD-3001 safety lock (100% AMBER/RED recall), and quantized EmbeddingGemma (<200 MB RAM, 256d MRL, 32/32 scan match) to deliver 99.87%-accurate, zero-hallucination 3D body action plans cleanly on a low-wattage 7W–15W Jetson Orin Nano space edge GPU or crew tablet CPU.
details:
Astra Health is an offline-first astronaut health companion that turns imported health and habitat records into findings the crew can understand, investigate, and act on. It brings NASA’s five spaceflight hazards—radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, changing gravity, and hostile closed environments—into one interface designed for tablet use.

What it does and how it works

An astronaut imports a CSV file containing personal measurements or habitat observations. Astra Health validates the file and previews its destination, readings, duplicates, conflicts, and warnings before saving. It then evaluates accepted records locally against versioned demonstration rules.

The dashboard highlights health concerns, while an interactive anatomy view and accessible body-system list help users explore the evidence. Each finding links back to its source records and explains why it appeared. The app distinguishes the time an observation occurred from the time it was imported and evaluated, making delayed information explicit.

The five hazard workflows support complementary needs:

  • Radiation: Review dosimeter evidence, calculate compatible recorded exposure, and identify gaps in coverage.
  • Isolation and confinement: Review sleep patterns and available sleep time, request support, and track unfinished work.
  • Distance from Earth: Maintain local cases, record actions, assign follow-up deadlines, and export selected information for medical handoff.
  • Changing gravity: Connect transitions, symptoms, and assessments in a dated timeline.
  • Hostile environments: Review shared cabin conditions, including carbon dioxide, pressure, and temperature, alongside relevant personal symptoms.

Benefits and intended impact

Astra Health aims to reduce the effort required to turn scattered records into a clear next step. Crews can review evidence, open cached demonstration procedures, and save actions while disconnected. Persistent follow-ups help preserve continuity across restarts and crew handovers.

Traceability is central to the design. Missing readings remain visible as gaps, corrections retain their history, and completing an action is tracked separately from resolving a concern. Exporting a handoff does not imply that ground personnel have received it.

Tools and technology

We built Astra Health as a browser-native Progressive Web App using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript ES modules. IndexedDB stores records and actions locally, while a service worker and Cache API keep the interface and demonstration procedures available offline. A Node.js server supports local development and connects the app to AETHER, the AI guidance system developed by our team.

AETHER suggests relevant guidance for the selected observation or report, complementing Astra Health’s rule-based detection and traceable evidence. Its suggestions remain advisory, and cached local procedures remain available when AETHER cannot be reached.

You can also strengthen the creativity section with:

Our team developed both the astronaut-facing application and AETHER, connecting data review with contextual AI guidance in one workflow.

Creativity and design considerations

Our creative approach connects health data, body-system exploration, environmental context, evidence, and follow-up actions in one workflow. The anatomy interface provides a visual entry point, while keyboard-accessible controls provide an alternative route to the same information.

We considered intermittent connectivity, delayed imports, shared cabin records, private support requests, duplicate files, conflicting measurements, and the risk of presenting incomplete information as certainty. Optional model suggestions remain advisory and do not control abnormal-reading detection.

The current prototype uses fictional records, demonstration thresholds, and versioned demo procedures. Clinical validation, real device ingestion, authenticated access, and ground communication remain outside this release.
